text:
customer-ops: Hey team, customer reported sudden 403s from mobile clients starting 10:12 UTC after we rotated the prod API key this morning. They say retries don't help, and errors started immediately after rotation.

sam: @customer-ops can you grab an example request-id + the Authorization header from the failing mobile request? Also which mobile-sdk version are they on?

customer-ops: request-id: req_0a9f7b2c, header: Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED. SDK v1.3.2. Server-side edge-proxy log shows `auth: invalid api key` for that request-id.

rita: Quick Q — does the mobile app fetch keys from a config endpoint or embed them? Usually mobile should use ephemeral tokens but some customers still fetch a long-lived key.

customer-ops: They fetch from our config-service endpoint which returns the api key. The config-service reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from env (mount from Vault via agent). We rotated in Vault, but we did a rolling deploy of config-service and expected zero downtime. Mobile caches config for up to 24h, but they report failures immediately — looks like some clients got a revoked key.

sam: Two possibilities: 1) config-service picked up a rotated value with a subtle formatting change (whitespace/newline) that the SDK rejects, 2) config-service had mixed replicas — some serving old key and some serving new revoked key after rewrap failed. Can you paste relevant logs (vault-agent, config-service, kms)?

customer-ops: Logs snippet: 
```
vault-agent: INFO fetched secret version v3 for path secret/data/apikeys/prod
config-service: INFO env REDWOOD_API_KEY set
auth: WARN failed unwrap KMS: InvalidCiphertext
edge-proxy: ERRO auth.go:87 invalid api key for request req_0a9f7b2c
```

hana: That KMS InvalidCiphertext is interesting — suggests one replica failed to unwrap the new cipher blob and fell back to a cached old secret or an intermediate. If the old key was revoked at rotation time that would explain 403s. Also, mobile caching plus config-service serving mixed keys creates a short window of chaos.

rita: Also flag: we've seen a helm templating issue before where secrets written into env had a trailing newline because of `|` vs `>-` in the template. The SDK does strict token compare and will 403 on a mismatched value (even trailing \n). Search for trailing newline in the env.

sam: @customer-ops can you exec into the config-service pod and run:
```
kubectl exec -c app -it $(kubectl get pods -l app=config-service -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- sh -c "printenv | grep REDWOOD"
```
and paste output? Also try `kubectl rollout restart deployment/config-service` after we confirm.

customer-ops: ran it. Output shows: `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-rotated-XXXXX\n` — there is a literal trailing newline in the env value (looks like the secret string includes a newline). We restarted the deployment and the restarted pods show `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-rotated-XXXXX` (no \n). After the restart, mobile clients started recovering within ~2 minutes as they requested fresh config.

hana: That lines up — root cause = helm/vault templating wrote a newline into the env which made the new key string not match the expected token, causing token validation to fail and be treated as revoked/invalid. Recovery steps: 1) restart config-service pods to pick up the sanitized env (done), 2) bump config API version to force clients to refresh before TTL expires, 3) add a short-lived grace allowlist in edge-proxy for the old key when rotating next time, 4) add a lint check in our helm charts to strip trailing newlines from secret values.

rita: Also recommend adding a small probe after rotation that hits config-service and validates the key via the same auth path clients use (end-to-end check).

sam: Great triage. customer-ops please add the unwrap/KMS error to the ticket and note the helm templating fix. Marking this as resolved after prod verification. :thumbsup:

customer-ops: Confirmed recovery and customers are green. Will file the helm chart patch and E2E post-rotation check. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
